_comment: Applicant-identity verdicts, keyed by a digest of the text itself so the same sentence is judged once wherever it appears. Written by ETL/terms/classify_applicant_identity.py; read by web/scripts/check_applicant_identity.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD on a published eligibility_text judged `beneficiary_not_applicant`. Do not hand-edit a verdict: fix the TEXT so it states the applicant's own test, or withdraw it.
_property: A published eligibility text is shown to a founder under the heading "who may apply". Judge, AS A WHOLE, WHOSE test it states, in whatever language it is written.  Two different populations can appear in such a text:   * the entity that would SUBMIT the application and sign the funding contract, and   * the entity that ultimately BENEFITS from what the money buys.  In most schemes these are the same population and the distinction does not arise. In a DELIVERY scheme they are different: the money pays an intermediary -- an adviser, an operator, an animator, a relay or technical-assistance body -- to do something for a downstream population, and that downstream population cannot apply.    applicant                  -- the population the text describes is the one that would submit and sign. This is the normal case. It stays `applicant` when the text also mentions who will ultimately be served, so long as the population being TESTED is the applicant's.    beneficiary_not_applicant  -- the population the text puts forward as its subject is a downstream one, served by the money rather than applying for it. A reader who matches the description would not be an eligible applicant. This is true however accurate the sentence is about the scheme.    indeterminate              -- the text states a subject matter, a theme or a project type without identifying any population at all, so there is nothing to place on either side.  THE TEST, applied to the population the text describes: could a reader who matches it sign the funding contract? If the text describes the people the scheme is FOR while the money would be paid to somebody else who serves them, the answer is no and the verdict is `beneficiary_not_applicant`.  Two things that do NOT make a text `beneficiary_not_applicant`. Naming the final audience alongside a clear statement of who submits -- that is an applicant test with context. And a scheme whose applicants happen to be advisers, consultancies or public bodies IN THEIR OWN RIGHT, where the text is their test and they are the ones applying. The defect is a MISMATCH between the population described and the population that may apply, not the presence of an intermediary anywhere in the sentence.
